sections.title: Bank Operating Metrics
sections.subtitle: Margin, efficiency, capital and asset quality -- the metrics that drive a bank's valuation more than revenue growth does

charts.title: Net Interest Income & Net Fee Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

nim.title: Net Interest Margin
nim.content:
Net Interest Margin (NIM) is net interest income divided by average interest-earning assets -- the spread a bank earns lending and investing versus what it pays for deposits and wholesale funding.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: NIM expanded through 2022-2023 as rates rose, then has been compressing back down through FY2025/FY2026 as rate cuts and deposit competition bite -- it is the single biggest swing factor in DBS's net interest income.

What to watch:

  • Direction of NIM relative to the rate cycle (DBS is a net asset-sensitive lender)
  • NIM compression outpacing loan growth, which would shrink net interest income even as the balance sheet grows

costToIncome.title: Cost-to-Income Ratio
costToIncome.content:
Cost-to-income ratio is operating expenses divided by total income -- the bank-specific efficiency measure that replaces operating margin.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: DBS runs in the low-to-mid 40s%, among the better ratios of the Singapore banks; a sustained move above the mid-40s would signal technology or headcount spend outrunning income growth.

What to watch:

  • Ratio drifting up even as income grows (cost discipline loosening)
  • Step-changes from one-off restructuring or technology investment versus a structural trend

cet1.title: CET1 Ratio
cet1.content:
Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio is the bank's core equity capital divided by risk-weighted assets -- the regulator's primary measure of loss-absorbing capacity. It is FY-only here because MAS disclosure of the ratio is annual/semi-annual, not every quarter.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: DBS targets a CET1 buffer comfortably above the MAS minimum (around 17% currently), which is also the capital base its capital-return and buyback decisions are measured against.

What to watch:

  • Ratio falling toward management's stated operating range, which would pressure buybacks/dividends
  • Risk-weighted asset growth outpacing capital generation

npl.title: Non-Performing Loan Ratio
npl.content:
NPL ratio is non-performing loans as a percentage of gross loans -- the headline asset-quality indicator for a lender.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: DBS has kept NPL around 1.0% through the current cycle, low by regional standards; it is the number to recheck first if China property or SME stress resurfaces.

What to watch:

  • Any upward inflection, even from a low base, ahead of a credit cycle turn
  • NPL ratio versus the credit impairment charge -- rising charges with a flat ratio can mean provisioning ahead of recognised stress, or the reverse

loansDeposits.title: Net loans and customer deposits
loansDeposits.content:
Net loans & advances and customer deposits are the two sides of the core banking book -- loans are the main earning asset, deposits the main (and cheapest) funding source.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: deposits have run ahead of loans in recent periods, which is why the loan-to-deposit ratio has eased even as both book sides grow -- a comfortable funding position, though it also means more low-yielding liquid-asset carry.

What to watch:

  • Loan growth re-accelerating relative to deposits (loan-to-deposit ratio rising)
  • Deposit mix shifting from low-cost CASA to higher-cost fixed deposits, which would pressure NIM independent of rates

roeRoa.title: Return on Equity and Return on Assets
roeRoa.content:
ROE is net income over average shareholders' equity; ROA is net income over average total assets. Together they separate how profitable the balance sheet is (ROA) from how much leverage is being used to amplify that into a shareholder return (ROE).

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: DBS has sustained high-teens ROE through FY2023-FY2025, among the best of any major bank globally, on an ROA near 1.3% -- the gap between the two is a function of the bank's leverage, which is itself regulated by the CET1 ratio above.

What to watch:

  • ROE declining toward its cost of equity rather than away from it
  • ROA trend in isolation from leverage, since ROE can hold steady while ROA erodes if capital buffers quietly thin

revenueMix.title: Net interest income and net fee & commission income
revenueMix.content:
Net interest income is interest earned on loans and investments less interest paid on deposits and funding; net fee & commission income is wealth management, cards, trade and transaction-banking fees -- the two largest lines of total income for a universal bank.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: net interest income is still the majority of revenue and is the line most exposed to the NIM chart above; fee income (wealth management in particular) is the diversification story management points to when rates are falling.

What to watch:

  • Fee income growing share of the mix, which would reduce DBS's rate sensitivity over time
  • Both lines falling together, which points to volume/activity weakness rather than just a rate effect

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For DBS Group Holdings Ltd: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
